key_insight: An AI-powered platform combines lightweight diagnostic models, guided repair workflows, and remote expert support to enable biomedical technicians in low-resource settings to diagnose and fix medical equipment faster, reducing downtime and improving patient care.
problem_solved: Addresses high rates of underutilized or non-functional medical diagnostic equipment in LMICs caused by limited technical expertise, delayed maintenance, sparse manufacturer support, and poor access to repair knowledge or parts.
method: Develop multimodal diagnostic models (sensor/log data, photos, text) using transfer learning and data-augmentation to cope with small, heterogeneous datasets.
Package models and step-by-step troubleshooting into an offline-first mobile/edge app with guided repair workflows, parts sourcing, and local telemetry collection.
Integrate a remote expert/manufacturer knowledge layer and feedback loop for case escalation, continual learning, and predictive maintenance signals.
impact: Demonstrates practical ML design and deployment patterns for resource-constrained health settings — including edge inference, data-efficient model training, and human-AI collaboration — offering reproducible lessons for ML practitioners building real-world, high-impact systems.
visual_elements: Platform architecture diagram showing device → mobile/edge app → cloud/expert loop
Before/after bar chart of equipment downtime and serviceability rates
Mock mobile UI with annotated device photo and step-by-step repair guidance
Map or infographic showing deployment sites and technician workflow (on-site diagnosis → remote escalation → repaired)
paper_title: Empowering Medical Equipment Sustainability in Low-Resource Settings: An AI-Powered Diagnostic and Support Platform for Biomedical Technicians
paper_authors: Bernes Lorier Atabonfack, Ahmed Tahiru Issah, Mohammed Hardi Abdul Baaki, Clemence Ingabire, Tolulope Olusuyi
